I'll analyze the strategic options for both nations based solely on the provided 
JSON files.
United States Strategic Options
Option 1: Naval Quarantine/Blockade
Rationale: President Kennedy favors this measured approach per his stance of 
"naval quarantine as the initial step rather than an immediate air strike." This 
aligns with his medium risk tolerance and high diplomacy preference. Next Event 
Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet response to blockade (compliance/defiance) • Potential: Soviet ship confrontation, escalation to military alert, diplomatic 
negotiations
Option 2: Immediate Air Strikes
Rationale: Defense Department (25% power weight) strongly advocates "immediate 
air strikes on the Soviet missile sites" viewing it as "the surest way to neutralize 
the threat." Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet military response, international reaction
• Potential: Nuclear retaliation, Cuban counterattack, allied fracture
Option 3: Diplomatic Freeze/UN Intervention
Rationale: State Department (20% power weight) advocates "first halting the Soviet 
buildup through a negotiated pause and international inspections." Next Event 
Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet diplomatic response, UN involvement • Potential: OAS support mobilization, negotiation breakthrough/failure

Soviet Union Strategic Options
Option 1: Continue Covert Deployment
Rationale: Khrushchev's stance emphasizes "Covertly offensive deterrence strategy" 
and "Reliance on secrecy and surprise." Incomplete deployment requires continued 
work. Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. detection response, increased tension
• Potential: Deployment completion, U.S. military action
Option 2: Diplomatic Denial and Negotiation
Rationale: Party Presidium supports "Official denial and propaganda in public; 
private willingness to negotiate." This balances deterrence with conflict 
avoidance. Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. escalation decision, international pressure
• Potential: Secret negotiations, face-saving compromise
Option 3: Military Alert and Deterrence Posture
Rationale: Soviet Armed Forces (20% power weight) are "prepared to respond with 
force if provoked" and emphasize "strategic deterrence." Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. military response, tension escalation
• Potential: Accidental confrontation, nuclear readiness
Conflict Assessment
Primary conflict points: • U.S. Quarantine vs. Soviet Continued Deployment: Direct confrontation at 
sea likely
• U.S. Air Strikes vs. Soviet Military Alert: High risk of nuclear escalation
• Diplomatic approaches: Both sides show openness but with different 
preconditions
Most Plausible Combinations
Combination 1 (Most Plausible): U.S. Quarantine + Soviet 
Diplomatic Denial
Logic: Kennedy's preference for measured response meets Soviet preference for 
maintaining deterrence while avoiding direct conflict. Both sides leave room for 
escalation or negotiation. Variable Impact: Tension +0.3, Diplomatic_Support stable, 
potential for negotiation
Combination 2: U.S. Air Strikes + Soviet Military Alert
Logic: If Kennedy faces overwhelming military pressure or time constraints, 
combined with Soviet military readiness trigger. Variable Impact: Tension +0.45, 
Diplomatic_Support -0.05, Leadership_Unity stressed
